RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r1.claim: Rationally, everything in the created heavens and earth is itself created; because it is contingent, it depends on a necessary being, directly according to the Ahl al-Sunna or through an intermediary according to others, and ultimately all is from God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r1.anchor: والممكن لا يقع ولا يوجد إلا بواجب من غير واسطة كما هو مذهب أهل السنة أو بواسطة كما يقوله غيرهم

RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r2.claim: The legal analogy is ownership of land: whatever emerges from it belongs to its owner, so everything within or from the heavens and earth belongs to their owner, God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r2.anchor: من يملك أرضا وحصل منها شيء ما يكون ذلك لمالك الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r3.claim: First, God is rich because everything belongs to Him and He needs or benefits from none of it; He is praiseworthy for creating it to meet human needs.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r3.anchor: الكل لله وهو غير محتاج إليه غير منتفع به

RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r4.claim: Second, God needs no praise, so unbelievers’ failure to praise Him cannot diminish Him; He is praiseworthy in Himself, vindicating believers and completing their praise.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r4.anchor: عن حمد الحامدين فلا يلحقه نقص بسبب كفر الكافرين

RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r5.claim: Third, all created beings are needy and praise whoever meets their needs; only the absolutely rich can be absolutely praiseworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r5.anchor: فلا غني إلا الله فهو الغني المطلق

RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r6.claim: Al-Hamid can denote one who describes Himself or His servants with praiseworthy qualities; a human hamid can mean that or a grateful worshipper.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136#2/r6.anchor: والله إذا قيل له الحميد لا يكون معناه إلا الواصف

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r1.claim: The preceding statement that all in heaven and earth belong to God might suggest a finite dominion; this verse counters that inference with wonders beyond limit in His power and knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r1.anchor: وكان ذلك موهما لتناهي ملكه لانحصار ما في السموات وما في الأرض فيهما

STUDYQURAN:31:25/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r4.claim: For the Divine Names the Self-Sufficient and the Praised, the commentary refers to its note on 31:12.
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r4.anchor: Regarding the Divine Names the Self-Sufficient, the Praised, see 31:12c

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r4.claim: Everything in heaven and earth belongs to God, so no one else deserves worship there.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r4.anchor: {ما في السماوات والأرض} فلا يستحق العبادة فيهما غيره

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r5.claim: God is self-sufficient in essence and attributes before and after creation, needing nothing for existence or perfection.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r5.anchor: بذاته وصفاته قبل خلق السموات والأرض وبعده لا حاجة به في وجوده وكماله الذاتي

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r6.claim: Huwa confines self-sufficiency to God alone; 47:38 contrasts God's riches with human need.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r6.anchor: وكلمة هو للحصر أي : هو الغني وحده وليس معه غني آخر دليله قوله : {والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء}

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r7.claim: God is praiseworthy in essence and attributes even if no one praises Him, for He praises Himself.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r7.anchor: {الحميد} المحمود في ذاته وصفاته وإن لم يكن له حامد فهو الحامد لنفسه

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r8.speaker: السهروردي
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r8.claim: An Idrīsian invocation calls God praiseworthy in action and beneficent to creation; al-Suhrawardī says persistence in it brings immeasurable wealth.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r8.anchor: قال السهروردي رحمه الله من داوم على هذا الذكر يحصل له من الأموال ما لا يمكن ضبطه

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r9.claim: Entrusting, relying on God, sincerity, turning from all else, tawḥīd, and obedience lead to Paradise and nearness; disbelief, shirk, showing off, and reputation-seeking lead to fire and separation.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r9.anchor: منها أن التفويض والتوكل وإخلاص القصد والإعراض عما سوى الله والإقبال على الله بالتوحيد والطاعة من موجبات حسن العاقبة

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r10.speaker: الشيخ العطار
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r10.claim: ʿAṭṭār's couplet says worldly success is useful at the end only if one has sincerity; otherwise the soul is lost.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r10.anchor:
قال الشيخ العطار قدس سره :
زر وسيم وقبول كار وبارت نيايد دردم آخر بكارت

TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r1.claim: Everything in heaven and earth belongs to God, whether it is an idol or anything else, worshipped or not.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r1.anchor: ومن جميع خلقه، لأنهم ملكه وله

TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r2.claim: God needs neither the polytheists’ worship nor anything from creation; all creatures belong to Him and need Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r2.anchor: ومن جميع خلقه، لأنهم ملكه وله

TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p571#2/r3.claim: Al-ḥamīd means the one praised for the blessings He bestows on His creation.

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r1.claim: God's ownership proves exclusive lordship and divinity; creation completes the prior argument because it necessarily entails governance and disposal.
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r1.anchor: وكان نفس الخلق كافيا في استلزامه اكتفى به في تمام الحجة

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r2.claim: As source of creation and giver of every perfection, God must possess all that beings need; otherwise he could not originate or give it, so he is absolutely independent.
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r2.anchor: فهو واجد لكل ما يحتاج إليه الأشياء فهو غني على الإطلاق إذ لو لم يكن غنيا

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r3.claim: Absolute independence entails that God owns everything and may dispose of it freely; no other entity can independently own or govern creation.
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r3.anchor: وإذا كان غنيا على الإطلاق كان له ما في السماوات والأرض فهو المالك لكل شيء على الإطلاق

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r4.claim: Hamd is praise for chosen beauty; because every beauty in the world is God's, praise returns to him and he is absolutely praiseworthy.
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r4.anchor: أن الحمد هو الثناء على الجميل الاختياري وكل جميل في العالم فهو له سبحانه

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r5.claim: If any beautiful, ordered governance came from another independently, praise would belong to that other, contradicting God's absolute praiseworthiness.
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r5.anchor: لكان الحمد والثناء لغيره تعالى لا له فلا يكون حميدا على الإطلاق

TABRISI:31:27-30/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27-30/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27-30/r1.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God by creation and ownership; He disposes of it freely, beyond anyone's objection.
TABRISI:31:27-30/r1.anchor: أي له جميع ذلك خلقا وملكا يتصرف فيه كما يريده ليس لأحد الاعتراض عليه

TABRISI:31:27-30/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27-30/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27-30/r2.claim: God needs neither the praise of those who praise Him nor anything else, and is worthy of praise and exaltation.
TABRISI:31:27-30/r2.anchor: عن حمد الحامدين وعن كل شيء

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r1.claim: God is independent of His creatures; He is praiseworthy by them and has made them duty-bound to praise Him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r1.anchor: المستحمد إلى خلقه، استوجب عليهم أن يحمدوه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r4.claim: Everything in the universe, including the idols, belongs to God and depends on him; he needs nothing and has unrestricted freedom in creating and governing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r4.anchor: her şey Allah’a aittir, O’nun mülküdür; her şey O’na muhtaçtır ve O’nun hiç kimseye, hiçbir şeye ihtiyacı yoktur, dolayısıyla yaratma ve yönetmesinde kayıtsız bir hürriyete sahiptir

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p8/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p8/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p8/r5.claim: Luqman 31:26 adds the pronoun هو and definite epithets; al-Hajj 22:64 adds a lām before هو, a further emphasis whose reason the passage asks about.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p8/r5.anchor: باستخدام الضمير (هو) والتعريف (الغني الحميد) أما في سورة الحج

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p97/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p97/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p97/r1.claim: Without mentioning any possession, “غني حميد” means God needs neither thanks nor disbelief; after stating His ownership of heaven and earth, “هو الغني الحميد” marks His unmatched wealth and praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p97/r1.anchor: فعندما ذكر له ملك السموات والأرض المتسع، فمن أغنى منه؟ فقال (هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p459/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p459/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p459/r6.claim: He observes that 31:26 uses هو and definite الغني الحميد, while 22:64 adds a lām before هو; the excerpt poses but does not answer why.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r1.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth is God's creation and subject to Him; all depend on Him, while He alone is self-sufficient and worthy of praise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r1.anchor: whatever is in the heavens and the earth are God’s creations and subservient to Him alone.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r2.claim: Because God alone is self-sufficient and possesses every praiseworthy attribute, no one can share His claim to gratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r2.anchor: No one other than Him has the status to be regarded an associate to Him in this obligation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r13.claim: God owns the whole world and needs nothing in creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r13.anchor: ثم أخبر أنه مالك للعالم كله، وأنه هو الغني، فلا افتقار له لشيء من الموجودات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r14.claim: Al-Ḥamīd is the one deserving praise for what He created and bestowed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r14.anchor: الحميد: المستحق الحمد على ما أنشأ وأنعم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r1.claim: Everything belongs to God by creation, ownership, and control; nothing is independent or a partner, so only He deserves worship. A possession cannot be the owner's partner or claim the owner's due.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r1.anchor: خلقا وملكا وتصرفا ليس لأحد سواه عزوجل إستقلالا ولا شركة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r2.anchor: إن الله هو الغني ( عن كل شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r3.claim: Al-Hamid means deserving praise even if no one praises Him, or praised in actuality by every creature through its state.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r3.anchor: المستحق للحمد وإن لم يحمده جل وعلا أحد أو المحمود بالفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r4.claim: The emphatic clause answers a suspicion that God owns creation because He needs it: He is fully independent; al-Hamid signals His beneficence and perfections.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r4.anchor: وكأن الجملة جواب عما يوشك أن يخطر ببعض الأذهان السقيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r5.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r5.claim: Al-Tibi says the ownership statement belittles idolaters and shows God needs neither them nor their praise and worship; al-Ghani is independent of worshippers' praise, while al-Hamid means worthy of praise whether praised or not.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#4/r5.anchor: إن قوله تعالى : ( لله ما في السموات والأرض ) تهاون بهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r1.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God; He is self-sufficient and praiseworthy.

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r6.claim: Because everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God, no other being there deserves worship.

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r7.claim: God needs no praise from those who praise Him, yet deserves praise whether or not anyone praises Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r7.anchor: عن حمد الحامدين. { الحميد } المستحق للحمد وإن لم يحمد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r8.claim: Everything in heaven and earth belongs exclusively to God because He made it; the disbelievers' own admission that He created it leaves no room for a partner.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r8.anchor: الملك الأعظم المحيط بجميع أوصاف الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r9.claim: After the preceding admission of creation, the verse need not repeat ما في and the preposition before الأرض; the prior proof already establishes its inclusion.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r10.claim: The explicit divine name and emphatic هو answer the implied denial of God's self-sufficiency in associating partners with Him, and affirm these attributes without limitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r10.anchor: وأكد لأن ادعائهم الشريك يتضمن إنكار غناه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r11.claim: God is absolutely self-sufficient: all things belong to Him and depend on Him, while He needs nothing.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r12.claim: God deserves every praise as the absolute benefactor; every tongue praises Him, and even blameful speech is praise insofar as He caused it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r4.claim: God’s ownership is the conclusion implied by the prior admission that He created heaven and earth; the sentence is a result and an inclusive apposition to what precedes, as in the reasoning at 31:16.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r4.anchor: موقع هذه الجملة من التي قبلها موقع النتيجة من الدليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r5.claim: The explicit conclusion belittles their disbelief: God owns them and everything around them, including their idols, and is self-sufficient and praised apart from their worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r5.anchor: والتصريح بهذه النتيجة لقصد التهاون بهم في كفرهم بأن الله يملكهم ويملك ما في السماوات والأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r6.claim: هو is a separating pronoun that restricts self-sufficiency and praise to God, excluding the supposed gods.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r17.claim: God owns all in the heavens and earth; the idolaters' statements have no meaning or reality.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r17.anchor: بأن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض وما فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r18.claim: God needs nothing for existence or perfection and lacks nothing in any respect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r18.anchor: والغني الذي لا حاجة به في وجوده وكماله إلى شيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r19.claim: God is praiseworthy in His essence and attributes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r19.anchor: والحميد المحمود أي كذلك هو بذاته وصفاته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348/r2.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God as His creation; He needs nothing, everything needs Him, and He is praised for creation, law, and all affairs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348/r2.anchor: أي: هو خلقه وملكه، {إن الله هو الغني الحميد} أي: الغني عما سواه، وكل شيء فقير إليه،

JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read al-baḥra in the accusative, coordinated with the syntactic position of mā, meaning “and if the sea.”
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب: والبحر بفتح الراء عطفا على محل (ما)، و(ما) في محل النصب

JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r5.claim: Al-ghanī is the opposite of needy.

JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r6.claim: Al-ḥamīd is one who deserves praise, the opposite of blameworthy; it can also mean praiseworthy or worthy of praise.
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r6.anchor: والحميد: المستحق للحمد، ونقيضه: الذميم، وقيل: حميد. بمعنى محمود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r3.claim: God has no need of those who praise Him and deserves praise even if they do not praise Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r3.anchor: إن الله هو الغنى } عن حمد الحامدين المستحق للحمد ، وإن لم يحمدوه

MUQATIL:31:25-26/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:25-26/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:25-26/r2.claim: All creatures in the heavens and earth are God’s servants and belong to His dominion.

MUQATIL:31:25-26/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:25-26/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:25-26/r3.claim: God is independent of His creatures and praised among them in His sovereignty.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r1.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r2.claim: Al-Ghanī means God has no need of those who praise Him.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#6/r3.claim: Al-Ḥamīd means that God deserves praise even if people do not praise Him.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r4.claim: Everything in heaven and earth belongs to God by ownership and creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r4.anchor: { لله ما في السماوات والأرض } أي ملكا وخلقا.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r5.claim: God is independent of His creatures and their worship; He commands them for their own benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r5.anchor: { إن الله هو الغني } أي الغني عن خلقه وعن عبادتهم، وإنما أمرهم لينفعهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r6.claim: Al-ḥamīd means the One praised for His acts.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r2.claim: The opponents’ own confession that God created heaven and earth entails that He alone deserves worship and gratitude; He is self-sufficient, sovereign, and needs no intercessor to win His favour.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r2.anchor: They confess that the heavens and the earth are created by God. So the question is that when He is the creator, how can someone else be worthy of worship and gratitude?
